s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging, pruritic, erythematous skin lesion with atrophic appearance
salient_findings: Band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis
Round vascular spaces lined by a single layer of endothelial cells
key_facts: Male patient in his early 70s
2-year history of skin lesion on the proximal portion of the left calf
Lesion is mildly pruritic
Lesion has been gradually enlarging
No identifiable cause for the lesion
Topical corticosteroids and antifungals applied for 2 months with no improvement
Physical examination reveals an atrophic appearance
Histopathology shows no grenz zone
Vascular channel endothelial cells are positive for CD34 and CD31
Vascular channel endothelial cells are negative for D2-40
No hemosiderin deposits found with Perls Prussian blue stain

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, pruritic, erythematous skin lesion

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the histopathological findings of band-like vascular proliferation and atypical endothelial cells

shortlist.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Shares similarities with the case's histopathological features, including vascular channel formation and endothelial cell positivity for CD34

shortlist.label: Dabska tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by similar vascular proliferation and endothelial cell morphology, despite being rare

shortlist.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical and histopathological features, including the presence of round vascular spaces lined by endothelial cells

raw.rationale: The histopathology shows band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis with no grenz zone and round vascular spaces lined by a single layer of endothelial cells, which is consistent with retiform hemangioendothelioma. The vascular channel endothelial cells are positive for CD34 and CD31 but negative for D2-40, which also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Kaposi's sarcoma typically has a more prominent inflammatory component and spindle cell proliferation, which is not described in the histopathology.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Angiosarcoma is a highly malignant tumor that typically presents with more atypia and mitotic activity, which is not mentioned in the histopathology.

rejected.label: Dabska tumor
rejected.why: Dabska tumor is a rare vascular tumor that typically presents with a distinctive histological appearance of hobnail endothelial cells, which is not described in the histopathology.

rejected.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
rejected.why: Epithelioid hemangioma typically presents with a more prominent epithelioid endothelial cell component and often has a distinct inflammatory component, which is not described in the histopathology.
